Pasadena Municipal Court was established in 1893. Pasadena Municipal courts will productively address problems affecting the locals and businesses in the city of Pasadena. Pasadena Municipal Court will devote itself to giving ideal municipal services responsive to the overall community and compatible with the city’s history, culture, and antique character. The court website had a Pasadena Channel that gives information about the meeting in the Council City, events, news conferences, and many more.

History And Background

Pasadena Municipal Court Was Established In 1923 After The City Voted To Create Its Own Municipal Court Separate From The Los Angeles County Court System. It Remained In Operation Until 2000 When The California State Government Reorganized And Consolidated The Municipal And Superior Courts In Each County. After This Reorganization, Pasadena Municipal Court Was Merged Into Los Angeles County Superior Court’s Eastern Judicial District. Even With The Merger, The courthouse" Pasadena Courthouse And Judicial Officers Retained The Name Pasadena Municipal Court.

Jurisdiction And Types Of Cases

As A Municipal Court, Pasadena Municipal Court Hears Misdemeanor Criminal Cases, Traffic Infractions, And Civil Cases Under $25,000 In The City Of Pasadena. This Includes Cases Involving Traffic Tickets, DUIs, Petty Theft, Vandalism, Municipal Code Violations, And Civil Claims Like Small Claims Cases. Serious Felony Cases Are Heard At The Los Angeles Superior Court Instead.

Court Locations And Hours

Pasadena Municipal Court Is Located At 300 E. Walnut Street, Pasadena, CA 91101. The Courthouse Is Open From 8:00am To 4:00pm Monday Through Friday, Except On Court Holidays. Night Court Is Also Held On Thursdays Until 8:00pm.

Going to Pasadena Municipal Court

If you have a case at Pasadena Municipal Court, here is what you need to know before going:

Getting a Citation or Summons

The process starts when you receive a citation from law enforcement or a summons to appear in court for a case against you. Read it carefully as it will have important information about your charges, rights, and when and where to appear in Pasadena Municipal Court.

Checking for Your Court Date

Your court date will be listed on your citation or summons. You can also look it up online through the court's case access system. Mark your calendar so you don't miss your court date or you may face additional charges.

Knowing Your Rights and Options

As a defendant, you have legal rights including the right to see the evidence against you, have a lawyer represent you, and go to trial. You can fight the charges, plead guilty and accept penalties, or pursue options like traffic school. Educate yourself on the options so you can make informed decisions.

Hiring an Attorney

Having a lawyer represent you can help ensure your rights are protected and increase your chances of a favorable outcome. Defense attorneys regularly work in municipal courts like Pasadena so they know the system and can advise you. Shop around to find an attorney within your budget.

What to Expect in Court

Come prepared on your court date. Bring any documents related to your case, dress respectfully, and arrive early to get through security. In the courtroom, wait for your case to be called then approach the judge when instructed. The judge will discuss the charges and your options. Be polite in all interactions.

Going to Trial

If you can't reach an agreement through a plea deal, your case may go to trial. The prosecution must prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt. Having an attorney is highly recommended for trial to handle evidence rules, question witnesses, and present your defense.

Paying Fines and Fees

If found guilty, you will have to pay any fines and fees ordered by the court. You can pay in person, by mail, by phone, or online. Failing to pay may result in additional penalties. Inform the court if you need an alternative payment plan.

Traffic Cases at Pasadena Municipal Court

Many people go through Pasadena Municipal Court for traffic ticket cases. Here's what to know:

Fighting a Traffic Ticket

You can contest a traffic citation by pleading not guilty and requesting a court trial. At trial, the officer must prove you committed the traffic violation. You can argue they don't have sufficient evidence or present defenses like mistaken identity.

Traffic School

For minor moving violations, you may be eligible to attend traffic school to dismiss the ticket and avoid points on your license. You must request traffic school at your court hearing and pay associated fees.

Appealing a Decision

If found guilty at trial, you can appeal the decision within 30 days. Appeals are heard by higher courts and focus on legal errors rather than reexamining the facts of the case.

Criminal Cases at Pasadena Municipal Court

Pasadena Municipal Court handles pre-trial proceedings and trials for misdemeanor criminal cases like DUIs, petty theft, vandalism, and assault. Here's an overview:

Misdemeanors vs. Felonies

Misdemeanors are less serious crimes with maximum jail sentences of 1 year. Felonies are more serious and heard at superior court. Pasadena Municipal Court only sees misdemeanor cases.

The Arraignment

The arraignment hearing is your first court appearance. You are formally read the charges and enter a plea of guilty, not guilty, or no contest. If pleading not guilty, a trial date is set.

Making a Plea

Consult with an attorney before making a plea. Pleading guilty immediately results in sentencing. Pleading no contest means you don't dispute the charges.

Pretrial Motions and Hearings

Your attorney can file motions arguing to dismiss the case, suppress evidence, or transfer venue before trial. Hearings are then held for a judge to issue rulings on the motions.

The Trial and Sentencing

During the trial, witnesses testify and evidence is presented. The judge or jury then decides your guilt. If found guilty, the judge orders your sentencing, such as fines, probation, community service, or jail time.

Pasadena Municipal Court Cost

Pasadena Municipal Court Cost depends upon the case type. For example, if a person involves in violation 8090, that is, Affray, the total fine is $375. If a person is involved in violation 3105, driving without an invalid License, the total fine is $225.

Pasadena Municipal Court Driving Safety Cost

Pasadena Municipal Court introduced Driving Safety Cost for the person charged with a definite misdemeanor under Title 7, Subtitle C, and Transportation code; while working on a motor vehicle, according to the law, they must be given safety training. For this Training, a person must not complete driving training within the past 12 months. Fill in your information and send it to the Pasadena Municipal Court mail address.

Pasadena Municipal Court Division

Pasadena Municipal Court Division consists of three primary divisions.

  • Civil Division
  • Prospection Division
  • Liability and Claims

Pasadena Municipal Court Docket

Pasadena Municipal Court Docket tells the schedule of the upcoming dockets. It gives information about the Date, Time, Docket, Court Room, and Judges. If you want the complete case information, click on view cases, and then case, defendant, offence, and all detail will appear.

Pasadena Municipal Court Virtual Court

Pasadena Municipal Court Virtual Court is a virtual hearing system introduced in COVID-19. The Court listened to all cases remotely via videoconferencing, and all case virtual hearings will be live streamed on YouTube, but recording is not allowed.

Pasadena Municipal Court Virtual Court Appearance Request

Pasadena Municipal Court Virtual Court Appearance Request can be done by filling out the form. Fill in your personal information and submit the form. The Pasadena Municipal Court will give you a response in 5 to 6 working days via phone or email.

Pasadena Municipal Court City Marshal office

Pasadena Municipal Court City Marshal’s office gives out municipal warrants provided outside the Court and helps other agencies give warrant issues to people in Pasadena.

Pasadena Clean Streets Community Service Program

Pasadena Clean Streets Community Service Program is a separate department and is not a part of Municipal Court. This service program had a task force that provided cleaning services to Pasadena and other municipal courts.

Pasadena Municipal Court Juveniles

Pasadena Municipal Court Juveniles means that if you got a fine due to violence and your age is under 17, you must pay the fine by visiting the Court with your parents or guardians. The child and his parents committed to giving their current address information to the Court. If they change their address, inform the Court; otherwise, they may be arrested.

FAQ

How many rules are there for Pasadena Municipal Court?

Pasadena Municipal Court rules consist of six local rules that everyone must be followed in the Court.

Does the City Attorney’s Office advise citizens on a legal matter?

No, the City Attorney’s Office does not advise citizens on a legal matter. They only represent as a municipal entity in the Pasadena Municipal Court.

Where did Pasadena Municipal Court City Marshall Office Operate?

Pasadena Municipal Court City Marshall Office operates its services in Harris and nearby countries.

What is Pasadena Municipal Court General Information?

Pasadena Municipal Court General Information gives some general information related to the case. It gives details about Court Dates, Fines, Family Violence, Juveniles, and Warrant Information.

How is the Family Violence offence paid?

A person involved in family violence may have to enter a plea in Court before the judge. After the plea, you can pay your fine in person, online, by mail, or by phone.

How can we get information for assistance in the warrant line?

You can get information for assistance in the warrant line by contacting them on the phone using 713-475-5559.

Which Clothes are not allowed in the Pasadena Municipal Court?

Proper Attire is necessary for the Court. Shorts, flip flops, tanks, and halter tops are not allowed in the Court.

What is the result if we do not pay the fine or do not appear in Court?

If any person fails to pay the fine on time and does not appear in Court, then the result is:

  • Driver’s License renewal is rejected
  • Vehicle Registration renewal is rejected
  • Extra fine and an arrest warrant are issued
